items.question: What does SIPANEL do?
items.answer: SIPANEL engineers and executes industrial envelope systems, including sandwich panel systems, Standing Seam and ZIP Tech roofing, aluminium cladding, and related technical coordination. The focus is not only supply, but also risk reduction through precise design, smart procurement, and engineered installation.

items.question: Is SIPANEL only a sandwich panel supplier?
items.answer: No. SIPANEL should be positioned as an engineering-first industrial envelope company. Sandwich panels are one part of the system, alongside waterproof roofing, aluminium cladding, shop drawing coordination, procurement planning, and controlled installation.

items.question: What does engineering-controlled execution mean?
items.answer: Engineering-controlled execution means reviewing the system before installation: drawings, quantities, accessories, waterproofing details, installation sequence, and quality checkpoints. This helps reduce leakage risk, material waste, delays, rework, and hidden cost.

items.question: How does SIPANEL reduce project risk?
items.answer: SIPANEL reduces risk by reviewing project conditions early, coordinating technical details, planning procurement accurately, and controlling installation through execution logic and inspection checkpoints.

items.question: What are sandwich panel systems used for?
items.answer: Sandwich panel systems are used for industrial walls, roofs, cold rooms, warehouses, factories, logistics centers, and insulated building envelopes. Their performance depends on panel selection, joint logic, accessories, flashing details, and installation quality.

items.question: How should the correct sandwich panel type be selected?
items.answer: Panel type should be selected based on building use, insulation requirements, environmental conditions, fire considerations, panel thickness, joint type, project geometry, and installation conditions. SIPANEL reviews these factors before procurement.

items.question: How can panel material waste be reduced?
items.answer: Panel waste can be reduced through layout review, quantity planning, cutting logic, accessory coordination, and shop drawing review before ordering materials.

items.question: Why are shop drawings important for panel projects?
items.answer: Shop drawings clarify panel layout, dimensions, accessories, flashing logic, joint details, quantities, and installation sequence before site execution. They help reduce coordination errors and rework.

items.question: What is Standing Seam roofing?
items.answer: Standing Seam roofing is a metal roofing system with raised seams and concealed fastening. When designed correctly, it supports stronger waterproofing behavior for industrial roofs by reducing direct fastener exposure and improving seam control.

items.question: What is ZIP Tech roofing?
items.answer: ZIP Tech roofing refers to a concealed fastening roof system approach used for industrial waterproof roofing applications. The final performance depends on drainage planning, seam coordination, flashing detail, and controlled installation.

items.question: Why do industrial roofs leak?
items.answer: Industrial roof leakage often comes from weak drainage planning, incorrect slope, poor flashing coordination, uncontrolled penetrations, exposed fastener issues, or installation sequence errors.

items.question: How can roof leakage risk be reduced before installation?
items.answer: Leakage risk can be reduced by reviewing roof slope, drainage paths, gutters, downspouts, flashings, overlaps, penetrations, edge details, and installation sequence before roofing starts.

items.question: What is aluminium cladding used for?
items.answer: Aluminium cladding is used for industrial facades, factory exteriors, architectural metal coverings, entrance volumes, and exterior renovation projects. Quality depends on layout control, fixing details, edge conditions, and installation accuracy.

items.question: Why does facade layout matter in cladding projects?
items.answer: Facade layout controls panel rhythm, joint alignment, opening coordination, edge details, visual consistency, and material waste. Weak layout control can create visible quality problems and execution delays.

items.question: What affects aluminium cladding cost?
items.answer: Cladding cost depends on material type, panel size, fixing system, facade geometry, openings, edge details, waste percentage, substructure needs, and installation complexity.

items.question: How can I request a quotation or technical consultation?
items.answer: You can use the RFQ form, call SIPANEL, send an email, or contact the team through WhatsApp. It is best to include project type, location, estimated area, project stage, and any drawings if available.

items.question: What information should I send for RFQ?
items.answer: Send your name, company, phone, project type, location, estimated area, project stage, main concern, and any available drawings or files. This helps the engineering team review the request more accurately.

items.question: Can I send drawings or project files?
items.answer: Yes. The RFQ form can support optional uploads such as PDF, JPG, PNG, and DWG files if backend file upload is enabled securely.

page_sections.intro: Industrial roof failures often begin before installation: weak drainage planning, unclear flashing details, exposed fasteners, or uncoordinated penetrations.

cards.title: Weak Drainage Planning
cards.description: Poor slope, gutter, or downspout coordination can create standing water and long-term leakage risk.

cards.title: Incorrect Flashing Details
cards.description: Edges, ridges, valleys, and wall connections need precise details before execution.

cards.title: Uncontrolled Penetrations
cards.description: Skylights, vents, ducts, and service openings create risk when not detailed correctly.

cards.title: Exposed Fastener Risk
cards.description: Incorrect fastening strategy increases the chance of water ingress and maintenance problems.

cards.title: Thermal Movement Issues
cards.description: Large roof surfaces need movement-aware detailing to avoid stress and deformation.

cards.title: Installation Sequence Errors
cards.description: Even good materials fail when installation sequence and quality checks are not controlled.
